short: The learned numbers inside a model.
detail: A model's parameters are the values it learned during training. More parameters usually mean a larger model file and more memory use, but parameter count alone does not prove that a model is better.

short: The files containing the learned parts of a model.
detail: Model weights are the stored learned values that software loads when it runs a model. They are often the largest files in a repository.

short: A way to make model weights smaller by storing them with fewer bits.
detail: Quantisation reduces memory and disk use, often making a model easier to run locally. It can also reduce quality, so smaller is not always better.

short: A file format commonly used to run language models locally.
detail: GGUF files are commonly used by llama.cpp and apps built around it, including many local model tools. A GGUF file often includes quantised model weights.

short: A common format for storing model weights safely.
detail: safetensors is a model weight file format widely used with Python machine-learning tools. It avoids some risks of older pickle-based PyTorch files.

short: Hugging Face's popular Python library for loading and running many models.
detail: Transformers is commonly used by developers and researchers. It is powerful, but it usually requires a Python setup rather than a simple desktop app.

short: Local model software often used with GGUF files.
detail: llama.cpp is a widely used runtime for running many language models on personal computers. Many desktop tools use it underneath.

short: A local model runner controlled mainly from the command line.
detail: Ollama can run supported local language models and exposes a local API. A Hugging Face model page does not always map directly to an Ollama model tag.

short: A desktop app for downloading and trying local language models.
detail: LM Studio is often beginner-friendly for testing GGUF language models because it provides a graphical interface.

short: How much text a model can consider at once.
detail: Context length is usually measured in tokens, not words. Longer context can require more memory, especially while generating text.

short: The part that turns text into tokens the model can process.
detail: A tokenizer splits text into pieces called tokens. The model sees tokens rather than raw words or characters.

short: A model tuned to follow instructions.
detail: An instruct model is usually better suited to tasks like answering questions, summarising, or following prompts than a raw base model.

short: A model tuned for back-and-forth conversation.
detail: A chat model is usually trained or tuned to respond in a conversational style. It may require a specific chat template to work properly.

short: A general model before instruction or chat tuning.
detail: A base model predicts text but may not behave like a helpful assistant. It is often used as a starting point for fine-tuning.

short: A model aimed at programming tasks.
detail: Code models are usually trained or tuned on programming text. Some are useful for code completion, explanation, or coding chat, but they still need the right files and tool route.

short: A model that turns text or other input into vectors for matching.
detail: Embedding models are often used for search, recommendations, clustering, and retrieval. They are not usually meant for normal chatbot conversation.

short: A model for generating, editing, or understanding images.
detail: Image models usually need specialist image software or Python libraries. A normal local chat app is usually not the right starting point.

short: A model for speech, sound, or audio tasks.
detail: Audio models may transcribe speech, classify sounds, or generate audio. They usually need specialist tooling rather than a normal chatbot interface.

short: A model that can work with more than one kind of input.
detail: A multimodal model might combine text with images, audio, or video. Check the model card carefully because the required tools can be different from ordinary text chat.

short: A model that reorders search results by relevance.
detail: A reranker is commonly used after a search step. It scores which results best match a query, so it is useful for search systems but not for ordinary conversation.

short: A model that assigns labels to input.
detail: A classifier might label text as positive or negative, detect a topic, or classify an image. It answers with categories rather than acting like a chat assistant.

short: The page has mixed or weak clues about what the model is for.
detail: When the type is unclear, check the model card and examples before downloading. The extension is avoiding a confident guess because the evidence does not point cleanly in one direction.

short: Extra training that adapts a model for a narrower purpose.
detail: Fine-tuning changes a model using additional examples. It can make a model better at a task, style, or domain.

short: Running a trained model to get an output.
detail: When you type a prompt and the model answers, that is inference. It is different from training the model.

short: Memory on a graphics card.
detail: VRAM is fast memory used by a GPU. Many local model tools use VRAM when available, but some models can also run partly or fully in system RAM.

short: The main memory in your computer.
detail: System RAM is used by the operating system and apps. Some local model setups can use system RAM when the model does not fit completely in GPU VRAM.

short: A 16-bit number format often used for model weights.
detail: FP16 uses about half the storage of FP32. It is common for GPU-based model use, but it can still require more memory than heavily quantised files.

short: A 16-bit number format often used by newer machine-learning hardware.
detail: BF16 has similar storage size to FP16 but different numeric behavior. Many model repositories report BF16 weights.

short: A common 4-bit GGUF quantisation label.
detail: Q4_K_M is often used as a practical balance between smaller file size and usable quality for local language models. It is still an approximation, not the original full-precision model.

short: A model that requires access approval or accepted terms.
detail: A gated Hugging Face model may require signing in, sharing contact information, or accepting licence terms before files can be downloaded.

short: The README-style description for a model.
detail: A model card often explains intended use, limitations, training notes, licence information, and examples. Quality and completeness vary by repository.

short: The model design or class used by loading software.
detail: Architecture describes the model's internal design or software class. It should only be reported when metadata or the model card supports it.

short: Hugging Face metadata describing the model's likely task.
detail: Pipeline tags are structured Hugging Face labels such as text-generation, feature-extraction, or text-to-image. They are useful but not always complete.

short: The rules attached to using or sharing the model.
detail: Licence metadata can be missing or incomplete. This extension explains detected licence fields but does not provide legal advice.

short: Using a model for business or paid work.
detail: Commercial use depends on the actual licence terms. Do not assume it is allowed unless the licence clearly permits it.
